properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 26 at 5:45PM MDT until July 26 at 8:45PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest Colorado, including the following
counties, Dolores and San Miguel.

* WHEN...Until 845 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 545 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Egnar.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 26 at 4:06PM MDT until July 26 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Ferris burn scar in...
Northwestern Dolores County in southwestern Colorado...
North Central Montezuma County in southwestern Colorado...

* Until 700 PM MDT.

* At 406 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Ferris Burn Scar. Between 0.2 and 0.6 inches
of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 4 inches
in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall will result in debris flow moving through the
Ferris Burn Scar. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding in and around the Ferris Burn
Scar.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around
the Ferris Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Ferris Burn Scar

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 26 at 4:02PM MDT until July 26 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Gold Mountain Burn Scar in...
Northwestern Hinsdale County in southwestern Colorado...
East Central Ouray County in southwestern Colorado...
Southwestern Gunnison County in west central Colorado...

* Until 700 PM MDT.

* At 402 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Gold Mountain Burn Scar. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow
moving through the Dexter, Cutler and Cow Creeks. The debris flow
can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding in and around the Gold
Mountain Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around
the Gold Mountain Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Ouray and the Gold Mountain Burn Scar
